questions.knowledge_point: Determining Whether a Given Set Is a Basis of the Column Space of a Matrix With Two Rows
questions.problem:
The matrix $D$ is given below. Let ${d}_{1}$, ${d}_{2}$, and ${d}_{3}$ be the respective columns of $D.$ Determine if $B=\text{{}{d}_{1},{d}_{2}\text{}}$ is a basis of $\text{Col}(D).$ If that is the case, find ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}$, where ${d}_{3}={x}_{1}{d}_{1}+{x}_{2}{d}_{2}.$

$$
D=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 1 \\ -1 & -7 & -17\end{aligned}]
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we reduce the matrix $D$ to reduced row echelon form (RREF):

$$
\begin{aligned}D & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 1 \\ -1 & -7 & -17\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & -8 & -16\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=(-\frac{1}{8}){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

From the matrix above, we see that the pivot columns are the $1$st and $2$nd columns. So, a basis of $\text{Col}(D)$ is ${{d}_{1},{d}_{2}},$ that is to say,

$$
B={[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -7\end{aligned}]}.
$$

Now, since the $3$rd column of the reduced matrix is a non-pivot column, then the entries in that column tell us the coefficients needed to express ${d}_{3}$ as a linear combination of all the other columns in the original matrix. So, we have

$$
{{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -17\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{d}_{3}}={{(3)}_{⏟}}_{{x}_{1}}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{d}_{1}}+{{(2)}_{⏟}}_{{x}_{2}}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -7\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{d}_{2}}.
$$

This gives us ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}=3\cdot 2=6.$

questions.problem:
The matrix $W$ is given below. Let ${w}_{1}$, ${w}_{2}$, and ${w}_{3}$ be the respective columns of $W.$
Determine if $B=\text{{}{w}_{1},{w}_{3}\text{}}$ is a basis of $\text{Col}(W).$ 
If that is the case, find ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{3}$, where ${w}_{2}={x}_{1}{w}_{1}+{x}_{3}{w}_{3}.$

$$
W=[\begin{aligned}2 & -6 & 4 \\ 4 & -12 & 9\end{aligned}]
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we reduce the matrix $W$ to reduced row echelon form (RREF):

$$
\begin{aligned}W & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -6 & 4 \\ 4 & -12 & 9\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 2 \\ 4 & -12 & 9\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-4){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-2){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

From the matrix above, we see that the pivot columns are the $1$st and $3$rd columns. So, a basis of $\text{Col}(W)$ is ${{w}_{1},{w}_{3}},$ that is to say,

$$
B={[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 4\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 9\end{aligned}]}.
$$

Now, since the $2$nd column of the reduced matrix is a non-pivot column, then the entries in that column tell us the coefficients needed to express ${w}_{2}$ as a linear combination of all the other columns in the original matrix. So, we have

$$
{{[\begin{aligned}-6 \\ -12\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{w}_{2}}={{(-3)}_{⏟}}_{{x}_{1}}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 4\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{w}_{1}}+{{(0)}_{⏟}}_{{x}_{3}}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 9\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{w}_{3}}.
$$

This gives us ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{3}=(-3)\cdot 0=0.$

questions.problem:
The matrix $V$ is given below. Let ${v}_{1}$, ${v}_{2}$,  ${v}_{3}$ and ${v}_{4}$ be the respective columns of $V.$
Determine if $B=\text{{}{v}_{1},{v}_{3}\text{}}$ is a basis of $\text{Col}(V).$ 
If that is the case, find ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{3}$, where ${v}_{2}={x}_{1}{v}_{1}+{x}_{3}{v}_{3}.$ 

$$
V=[\begin{aligned}-3 & 0 & -6 & -3 \\ 0 & 10 & 20 & 10 \\ 2 & 0 & 4 & 4\end{aligned}]
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we reduce the matrix $V$ to reduced row echelon form (RREF):

$$
\begin{aligned}V & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & 0 & -6 & -3 \\ 0 & 10 & 20 & 10 \\ 2 & 0 & 4 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=(-\frac{1}{3}){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 10 & 20 & 10 \\ 2 & 0 & 4 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 10 & 20 & 10 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{10}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

From the matrix above, we see that the pivot columns are the $1$st, $2$nd, and $4$th columns. So, a basis of $\text{Col}(V)$ is ${{v}_{1},{v}_{2},{v}_{4}}.$ 

Therefore, we conclude that $B={{v}_{1},{v}_{3}}$ is not a basis of $\text{Col}(V).$

questions.problem:
The matrix $R$ is given below. Let ${r}_{1}$, ${r}_{2}$,  ${r}_{3}$ and ${r}_{4}$ be the respective columns of $R.$
Determine if $B=\text{{}{r}_{1},{r}_{2},{r}_{3}\text{}}$ is a basis of $\text{Col}(R).$ 
If that is the case, find ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}\cdot {x}_{3}$, where ${r}_{4}={x}_{1}{r}_{1}+{x}_{2}{r}_{2}+{x}_{3}{r}_{3}.$ 

$$
R=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -3 & -2 \\ 3 & 5 & -7 & -8 \\ 4 & 6 & -10 & -10\end{aligned}]
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we reduce the matrix $R$ to reduced row echelon form (RREF):

$$
\begin{aligned}R & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -3 & -2 \\ 3 & 5 & -7 & -8 \\ 4 & 6 & -10 & -10\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -3 & -2 \\ 0 & 2 & 2 & -2 \\ 4 & 6 & -10 & -10\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-4){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -3 & -2 \\ 0 & 2 & 2 & -2 \\ 0 & 2 & 2 & -2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=(\frac{1}{2}){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -3 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 2 & 2 & -2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-2){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -3 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

From the matrix above, we see that the pivot columns are the $1$st and $2$nd columns. So, a basis of $\text{Col}(R)$ is ${{r}_{1},{r}_{2}}.$ 

Therefore, we conclude that $B={{r}_{1},{r}_{2},{r}_{3}}$ is not a basis of $\text{Col}(R).$
